To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MATRICS Consensed Cognitive Battery (MCCC) did not detect procognitive effects of the drug amphetamine in a sample of healthy adults.
AMPH effects on cognitive performance in healthy adults were detected only among certain subgroups of individuals and in certain cognitive domains, and not in the inclusive sample of healthy adults.

AMPH effects on MATRICS MCCB performance were only detected among specific subgroups of healthy adults and in specific cognitive domain scores, and that these subgroup and domain effects were significantly associated with personality characteristics associated with schizophrenia-linked genes and/or brain function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of potential cognitive enhancers for the treatment of schizophrenia.
the development of a new class of compounds that may be useful for the treatment of schizophrenia.
the identification of candidate drugs for the treatment of cognitive deficits in schizophrenia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MCCB was not able to detect the effects of AMPH on cognition in a healthy sample.
AMPH effects on cognitive domains were not detected in the overall sample and that the results in the subgroups were not consistent across cognitive domains.
, at least in this sample, the MCCB did not identify any cognitive effects of AMPH in healthy adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MCCB is a sensitive measure of cognitive performance, but is not a reliable predictor of drug effects on cognition in healthy adults.
the MCCB is a sensitive measure of AMPH's effects, but the effects are not consistent across all domains or individuals.
AMPH did not enhance cognitive performance in healthy adults and the effects observed in this study were likely due to placebo effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MCCB, while a useful measure for detecting cognitive deficits in schizophrenia, is not a sensitive enough measure for detecting cognitive enhancements in healthy adults.
cognitive enhancement in healthy subjects does not necessarily predict cognitive improvement in schizophrenia patients.
the MCCB may be useful in identifying candidate procognitive agents, but that the strategy of using healthy subjects is not straightforward.
